package_info.package_versions: maliciously tampered version released in late March 2023
package_info.why_malicious: The 3CXDesktopApp package was maliciously tampered with during its build process, resulting in the distribution of software containing embedded malicious code to end users. This code was not present in the original source and was introduced as part of a targeted supply chain attack, enabling threat actors to compromise the systems of 3CX customers.

execution_context.trigger: application runtime (after user launches the app)
execution_context.file_location: 3CXDesktopApp.exe (Windows) or corresponding binary in distributed application package
required_permissions: filesystem (write/read for payload download and execution)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: /* Malicious code injected into the 3CXDesktopApp binary enables the application to initiate outbound network connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure, download additional payloads, and potentially exfiltrate sensitive data. The code is not present in the original source and is only found in the tampered build artifacts. */
malicious_snippets.code_language: C++ (for native binary) and/or JavaScript (if Electron-based)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At application runtime, the injected code initiates outbound HTTPS connections to attacker-controlled domains, downloads additional payloads to the local filesystem, and may exfiltrate sensitive data, resulting in remote code execution and potential data compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is absent from the legitimate source repository and only appears in the distributed binaries, indicating unauthorized tampering during the build process. The application establishes outbound connections to domains unrelated to 3CX, which is highly anomalous for a desktop VoIP client.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate 3CXDesktopApp build should only communicate with official 3CX infrastructure for updates or VoIP services, and should not download or execute code from untrusted sources post-installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automatic update mechanisms may contact trusted vendor servers to check for updates, but these are well-documented, use signed payloads, and do not execute arbitrary code from unknown domains.
key_indicators: Presence of network communication code in distributed binaries not found in source code
Outbound HTTPS requests to non-3CX, attacker-controlled domains
Download and execution of additional payloads post-installation
Binary hash mismatches compared to official releases
Unexplained increase in binary size or embedded resources

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into the 3CXDesktopApp during the build process via a compromised CI/CD pipeline.
attack_chain.leads_to: Distribution of tampered application to end users

attack_chain.action: End users install and launch the tampered 3CXDesktopApp, which executes the embedded malicious code at runtime.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code initiates outbound network connections to attacker infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Malicious code downloads additional payloads and may exfiltrate sensitive data from the victim's system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential full compromise of victim systems

behavioral_signatures: Presence of code in distributed binaries not found in the official source repository
Unexpected outbound HTTPS connections from 3CXDesktopApp to non-3CX domains
Application downloading and executing additional payloads after installation
Unusual process spawning or file creation by 3CXDesktopApp
file_indicators: 3CXDesktopApp binaries with hash mismatches compared to official releases
Unexplained changes in application binary size or embedded resources
Presence of unknown DLLs or executables dropped by 3CXDesktopApp
network_indicators: Outbound connections from 3CXDesktopApp to attacker-controlled domains or IPs not associated with 3CX
Unusual DNS queries or HTTP(S) requests initiated by 3CXDesktopApp to untrusted endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Compare distributed 3CXDesktopApp binaries against official source and release hashes to identify unauthorized modifications. Monitor network traffic from 3CXDesktopApp for connections to non-3CX domains or IPs. Use file integrity monitoring to detect changes in application binaries and the appearance of unknown files. Employ behavioral analysis to flag applications that download and execute additional code or initiate unexpected network communications post-installation.
